Toro, I.C. (2021). Techno-economic assessment of solvent-based bitumen extraction technologies including in-situ electromagnetic heating. MSc thesis, Engineering Management, Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Alberta, Edmonton. https://ualberta.scholaris.ca/items/d529494e-17f5-4c21-860f-83e6b03d6eca

Loaded: whole-process techno-economics (capacity, capex per bbl/d, supply cost, discount rate, lifetime) for Nsolv-type solvent-only extraction (Ch. 2) and ESEIEH electromagnetic heating with solvent (Ch. 3), both 25,000 bbl/d bitumen, Aspen HYSYS + DCF models, Alberta, 2021 CAD. Energy use is printed only for ESEIEH (114 GJ/h electricity, 198 GJ/h heating duty); Nsolv energy only as cost components (in other-values). No absolute GHG intensities are printed; only reprinted pilot reductions vs SAGD (~50%). Supply costs are per bbl dilbit and include diluent and pipeline transport to Cushing, so they are not production costs. Base-case Nsolv capital is derived (59/0.13 FCI +15% working capital). No SAGD model numbers beyond reprinted comparisons (other-values). Locator: printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 13). Trap: Ch. 3 price year not stated (2021 assumed); heating duty vs fuel input ambiguous.
